## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py` (shared FROST GEMM epilogue emitter)
- `test/python/gemm/frost/test_epilogue_mod.py` (new)

## Summary

- Under fp32 compute, `_emit_binary_ext` now emits the `mod` epilogue op as `{new} = {a} % {b}`. CuTe DSL lowers `%` on
  Float32 vectors to `arith.remf`, which compiles to an exact fmodf. Before, `mod` was emitted as `a - b * trunc(a / b)`:
  `q = a / b` (`div.rn.f32`), `trunc(q) = floor(|q|) * (step01(q) - step01(-q))`, then `a - b * trunc(q)`.
- INT32 compute keeps the existing form (see "API and compatibility impact").
- New regression test `test_epilogue_mod_is_exact_fmod`, with the GEMM output as dividend (`mod_C_x`) and as divisor
  (`mod_x_C`), on the dense SM120 template and, on SM100-family GPUs, the dense SM100 template.

## Why

cuDNN's MOD is the C floating-point remainder, fmod: Frost's own test reference is `torch.fmod`, and native cuDNN returns
exact fmod on the same SM120 GPU apart from subnormals, which it flushes to zero (see Testing and "API and compatibility
impact"), e.g. `mod(2**25, -3) = 2` and `mod(3, inf) = 3`. The emitted form rounds the quotient before truncating it. The
truncation of the rounded quotient is exact, and ptxas contracts the final multiply-subtract into one FFMA, so the result is
fmod when `trunc(fl(a / b)) == trunc(a / b)`, with two exceptions listed in the last bullet: infinite divisors and exact
negative multiples. It is wrong otherwise:

- when `a / b` lies just below a nonzero integer and rounds up to it, the result is `fmod(a, b) - sign(a) * |b|`, a small
  value of the wrong sign. This is common with integer dividends and decimal divisors: `mod(k, 0.1f)` is wrong for every
  integer `k` tested, e.g. `mod(2, 0.1f) = -2.98e-8` instead of `0.09999997`;
- from `|a / b| >= 2**23` the rounded quotient has no fraction bits. Below `2**25` it is at most one away from
  `trunc(a / b)`, so about half of the results are off by `|b|`: `mod(2**25, -3) = -1` instead of `2`. From `2**25` it is a
  multiple of 4 or more, so results can also leave `(-|b|, |b|)`: `mod(5 * 2**27, 0.7f) = 17.83` instead of `0.3286`,
  `mod(2**40, 1.3f) = 20669` instead of `0.3476`. `mod(x, 2 pi)` for a phase `x` in `[1e6, 1e8]` was wrong for about a
  third of the values;
- `b = +-inf` gives NaN (`inf * 0`) instead of `a`, and exact negative multiples return `+0` instead of `-0` (`mod(-4, 2)`),
  although the truncated quotient is right in both cases; a quotient that overflows gives `-inf` instead of the remainder
  (`mod(1e38, 2**-100) = -inf`, fmod `0`).

Minimal reproducer (the new test): dense `sm120_matmul` through `jit_from_cudnn_graph` with
`CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2`, bf16 A/B, M = N = K = 128, fp32 intermediate and compute, fp32
output `y = mod(C, x)` (or `mod(x, C)`) with `x` an fp32 per-element aux. `A` is the identity, so `C` holds exactly the
chosen bf16 values. Values that differ bitwise from fmod on develop 24a8cd43:

| `mod(C, x)` operand group | wrong on develop |
|---|---|
| `k / 0.1f` rounds up to `10 k`, `k = 1..256` and `-1..-64` | 320 of 320 |
| `\|C / x\| >= 2**23` (`2**25 .. 3 * 2**50` by `-3, 0.7, 1.3, 2.9`) | 19 of 24 |
| `x = +-inf` | 8 of 8 (NaN) |
| exact negative multiples (`-0` expected) | 3 of 3 (`+0`) |
| `C / x` overflows | 2 of 2 (`-inf`) |
| `C mod 6.2831855`, `C` in `[1e6, 1e8]` | 79 of 256 |
| `x = 0` (NaN expected) | 0 of 2 |
| small quotients, `\|C / x\| <= 16` | 1 of 128 (`mod(-8, 0.5) = +0`) |

For `mod(x, C)`: 84 of 256 phases `x` in `[1e6, 1e8]` mod `bf16(2 pi)`, 3 of 3 large or overflowing quotients, and the same
signed-zero case. With this change every value matches fmod bitwise.

`arith.remf` is the right lowering: it states fmod semantics in the IR instead of approximating them. On SM120 and SM100 it
compiles to the exact fmodf expansion (a quotient estimate corrected through an exact FMA remainder, a reduction loop once
`|a / b| > 2**23`, and `copysign` for the sign of `a`), with no `div.rn.f32` and no floor (PTX counts under Testing). The
audit also ran it against `math.fmod` on 358,400 operand pairs on SM120, including `+-0`, subnormal, `+-inf` and NaN
operands, with no difference, and the random-operand sweep under Testing found none in 524,288 more. Patching the old form
(for example with a remainder correction step) would still need special cases for infinite divisors, quotient overflow and
signed zeros.

The change is outside `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/` because, since #1993, the epilogue op emitter exists only in the
shared `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`: both families' `generate()` call the shared `_emit_pointwise_dag`
(`sm120/epilogue_codegen.py:827`, `sm100/epilogue_codegen.py:498`), which, like the shared `generate_mainloop`, reaches it
through `_emit_op`. There is no per-family copy to fix instead.

Found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding G4.1).

## Related issues

None.

Related PRs from the same audit:

- #2022 (G4.4, INT32-compute epilogue ops): on SM120 it declines an INT32-compute `mod`, the case this PR leaves on the old
  form.
- These open PRs edit other hunks of the same shared `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`: #2018 (B09, comparisons
  in `_emit_binary_ext`), #2026 (G4.3, `relu_backward` in `_emit_binary_ext`), #2009 (B10, relu slope and clip in
  `_emit_binary_ext` and `_emit_op`), #2012 (G4.2, relu NaN propagation in `_emit_op`), #2025 (B11, tanh / elu / softplus in
  `_emit_op`), #2022 (`gen_index` in `_emit_op` and `_emit_pointwise_dag`), #2014 (B13, `_emit_round`) and #2013 (B14, the
  reduction AVG divisor). `git merge-tree` merges each of their current heads with this branch without conflicts.

## API and compatibility impact

- No API change. FlashInfer's exported Frost graphs contain no `mod`.
- Numerics: an fp32-compute `mod` now returns exact C fmod in every epilogue that reaches the emitter. On SM120 that is all
  six templates (dense and block-scale matmul, MoE grouped matmul and its swap-AB form, MoE grouped block-scale matmul and its
  swap-AB form) and the split-K reduction epilogue; SM120 has no mainloop fusion. Results that were already exact, such as
  the quotients below 10 drawn by the existing sweep, are unchanged except for the sign of exact-zero remainders.
- Native cuDNN parity (AGENTS.md Rule 9): on every operand group of the new test, FROST now gives the same bits as native
  cuDNN. They still differ on subnormals, and that predates this change: native cuDNN flushes subnormal operands and results
  to zero (a subnormal divisor gives NaN, a subnormal dividend or exact remainder gives `+-0`), while FROST computes exact
  fmod on them; develop's FROST kernel did not flush either. In the random-operand sweep under Testing every native
  difference from fmod is one of these subnormal cases. The new test does not pin subnormal behaviour.
- SM100: the emitter is shared, so the SM100 family's generated code changes the same way: every SM100 template epilogue,
  the split-K reduction epilogue and the `sm100_matmul_mainloop.py` mainloop-fusion transform (a `mod` with a scalar divisor
  on A or B). Both kinds were compile-checked for `sm_100a` on the SM120 host (see Testing); nothing ran on SM100 hardware.
  The new test's two SM100 cases (the dense SM100 template, gated by `requires_sm100`) give SM100 CI a bitwise check of the
  changed path; they compile for `sm_100a` but have not run. The existing SM100 `mod` case,
  `test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py::test_pointwise_mode_coverage[mod]` (quotients below about 10, bf16 output, tolerance
  5e-2, 0.2% mismatch budget), still exercises the path on SM100 CI but cannot detect this defect.
- INT32 compute is unchanged: a `mod` node with `compute_data_type=INT32` keeps the old form and still fails at build with
  the same `DSLRuntimeError` (`'arith.addf' op operand #1 must be floating-point-like, but got 'vector<8xi32>'`).
  INT32-compute epilogue ops are a separate audit finding (G4.4, #2022, which declines an INT32-compute `mod` on SM120).
  Emitting `%` there would select `arith.remsi`, whose zero-divisor and overflow cases are undefined.
- Performance: the fmodf expansion is longer than the old divide-and-floor sequence and adds a short data-dependent loop
  for `|a / b| > 2**23`. Only graphs with a `mod` node are affected. Not measured.
- Chains with `mod` render different kernel source, so their cached kernels are rebuilt once.

## Testing

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN
9.24, frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. All pytest commands from `test/python`.

Regression test, RED on develop (a copy of 24a8cd43's `python/cudnn` and `test/python` with only the new test added, own
kernel caches) and GREEN on this branch:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_epilogue_mod.py -rs
# develop 24a8cd43: 2 failed, 2 skipped in 0.52s
#   [sm120-mod_C_x] 432 of 16384 differ from fmod (per-group counts in the table above)
#   [sm120-mod_x_C] 88 of 16384 differ from fmod
# this branch:      2 passed, 2 skipped in 0.47s
# both: SKIPPED [2] needs a Blackwell-family GPU (100 <= SM < 120), have sm_120  (the sm100-* cases)
```

The SM120 cases are collected by `-k sm120`, the SM100 cases by `-k sm100`, and all four by `-k frost` and the default
`-m L0` sweep.

Related existing tests:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost -k sm120
# develop 24a8cd43: 1 failed, 1036 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected, 201 warnings in 292.75s
# this branch:      1 failed, 1038 passed, 82 skipped, 9791 deselected in 13.34s
#   (warm kernel cache, so the time is not comparable with the cold develop run)
```

The two extra passes are the new test's SM120 cases; its two SM100 cases are deselected. The one failure,
`test_matmul.py::test_sm120_epi_vec_clamp_and_stg_only`, fails the same way on develop (`_use_tma_store_epi(chain, cfg100)`
is False for the SM100 config on an SM120 GPU) and has no `mod`.

Host-side codegen tests that render epilogues and mainloop transforms through `_emit_op` (their SM100 GPU cases skip on
SM120):

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_multi_gemm.py gemm/frost/test_matmul_mainloop_fusion.py gemm/frost/test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py
# develop 24a8cd43: 22 passed, 493 skipped in 0.89s
# this branch:      22 passed, 493 skipped in 0.84s
```

Ad hoc checks (scripts not committed):

- Every SM120 path that reaches the emitter, values differing bitwise from fmod. GEMM results are small integers (exact);
  divisors alternate between `0.1f` and `U[0.5, 1.5)`, except in the two MoE block-scale rows, where they alternate between
  `0.1f` and random fp32 bit patterns:

  | SM120 path | develop | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | dense, scalar divisor (`0.1f`) | 24467 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, per-row divisor | 12218 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, per-column divisor | 12223 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, per-element divisor | 12216 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, in-chain divisor `mod(C, C * x)` | 7275 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, split-K 2 (reduction epilogue) | 12237 / 24576 | 0 |
  | MoE grouped matmul (NONE), E = 2 | 16285 / 32768 | 0 |
  | MoE grouped matmul (NONE), swap-AB | 16301 / 32768 | 0 |
  | MXFP8 dense block-scale matmul | 8154 / 16384 | 0 |
  | MXFP8 MoE grouped block-scale matmul (NONE), E = 2, per-element divisor | 23130 / 32768 | 0 |
  | MXFP8 MoE grouped block-scale matmul (NONE), swap-AB | 23191 / 32768 | 0 |

- Native cuDNN: the new test's two graphs built through the public graph API without the FROST opt-in (heuristic modes A and
  FALLBACK, plan list headed by `eng10_k24=25`), executed on the same operands: 0 values differ from fmod in every group.
- Random operands: 524,288 pairs through the new test's two graphs (16 draws of 16,384 per direction; `C` random finite
  normal bf16 values, `x` random fp32 bit patterns with a quarter replaced by near-integer quotients). This branch's FROST
  kernel matches fmod bitwise on all of them. Native cuDNN (same plan list) differs on 8,487, all subnormal cases: all 5,485
  subnormal divisors give NaN, and all 720 subnormal dividends and all 2,282 subnormal exact remainders of normal operands
  give `+-0` with the sign of fmod; none of the other 515,801 pairs differs. Develop's FROST kernel differs on 162,048 pairs,
  none of them a flush: it returns all 720 subnormal dividends exactly and no NaN for a subnormal divisor.
- `mod` with `compute_data_type=INT32` on the dense template: develop and this branch both fail at build with the same
  `DSLRuntimeError` (unchanged, see above).
- PTX instruction counts of the new test's SM120 kernel (`sm_120a`) and of the two SM100 kernels below (`sm_100a`, the two
  kernels' counts summed):

  | instruction | `sm_120a` develop | `sm_120a` this branch | `sm_100a` develop | `sm_100a` this branch |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `div.rn.f32` | 64 | 0 | 192 | 0 |
  | `cvt.rmi.f32.f32` (floor) | 192 | 0 | 576 | 0 |
  | `div.approx.f32` | 0 | 64 | 0 | 192 |
  | `cvt.rzi.f32.f32` | 0 | 128 | 0 | 384 |
  | `fma.rz.f32` | 0 | 64 | 0 | 192 |
  | `copysign.f32` | 0 | 64 | 0 | 192 |

- SM100 compile check (no launch: an `sm_100a` kernel cannot run here). The process runs the sm100 tree
  (`CUDNN_FRONTEND_GEMM_ARCH_FAMILY=sm100`, arch probe pinned to 100 as `gemm_test_utils.plan_as_sm100` does) and compiles,
  with `--gpu-arch sm_100a` and `CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma`, a dense `sm100_matmul` epilogue
  `mod(C, x)` with an fp32 per-element divisor and an `sm100_matmul_mainloop` graph with `mod(A, s)` for a scalar `s`. Both
  compile on develop and on this branch; the generated source on this branch emits `_op_0 = _ba0 % _bb0` and
  `_op_900 = _ba900 % _bb900`. The new test's two SM100 cases, built the same way from the test's own graphs, `Plan` helper
  and config, also compile for `sm_100a` and emit `_op_0 = _ba0 % _bb0`.

Not tested: SM100-family hardware (none available here), so the new test's SM100 cases have not run.

detail.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py` (shared FROST GEMM epilogue emitter)
- `test/python/gemm/frost/test_epilogue_mod.py` (new)

## Summary

- Under fp32 compute, `_emit_binary_ext` now emits the `mod` epilogue op as `{new} = {a} % {b}`. CuTe DSL lowers `%` on
  Float32 vectors to `arith.remf`, which compiles to an exact fmodf. Before, `mod` was emitted as `a - b * trunc(a / b)`:
  `q = a / b` (`div.rn.f32`), `trunc(q) = floor(|q|) * (step01(q) - step01(-q))`, then `a - b * trunc(q)`.
- INT32 compute keeps the existing form (see "API and compatibility impact").
- New regression test `test_epilogue_mod_is_exact_fmod`, with the GEMM output as dividend (`mod_C_x`) and as divisor
  (`mod_x_C`), on the dense SM120 template and, on SM100-family GPUs, the dense SM100 template.

## Why

cuDNN's MOD is the C floating-point remainder, fmod: Frost's own test reference is `torch.fmod`, and native cuDNN returns
exact fmod on the same SM120 GPU apart from subnormals, which it flushes to zero (see Testing and "API and compatibility
impact"), e.g. `mod(2**25, -3) = 2` and `mod(3, inf) = 3`. The emitted form rounds the quotient before truncating it. The
truncation of the rounded quotient is exact, and ptxas contracts the final multiply-subtract into one FFMA, so the result is
fmod when `trunc(fl(a / b)) == trunc(a / b)`, with two exceptions listed in the last bullet: infinite divisors and exact
negative multiples. It is wrong otherwise:

- when `a / b` lies just below a nonzero integer and rounds up to it, the result is `fmod(a, b) - sign(a) * |b|`, a small
  value of the wrong sign. This is common with integer dividends and decimal divisors: `mod(k, 0.1f)` is wrong for every
  integer `k` tested, e.g. `mod(2, 0.1f) = -2.98e-8` instead of `0.09999997`;
- from `|a / b| >= 2**23` the rounded quotient has no fraction bits. Below `2**25` it is at most one away from
  `trunc(a / b)`, so about half of the results are off by `|b|`: `mod(2**25, -3) = -1` instead of `2`. From `2**25` it is a
  multiple of 4 or more, so results can also leave `(-|b|, |b|)`: `mod(5 * 2**27, 0.7f) = 17.83` instead of `0.3286`,
  `mod(2**40, 1.3f) = 20669` instead of `0.3476`. `mod(x, 2 pi)` for a phase `x` in `[1e6, 1e8]` was wrong for about a
  third of the values;
- `b = +-inf` gives NaN (`inf * 0`) instead of `a`, and exact negative multiples return `+0` instead of `-0` (`mod(-4, 2)`),
  although the truncated quotient is right in both cases; a quotient that overflows gives `-inf` instead of the remainder
  (`mod(1e38, 2**-100) = -inf`, fmod `0`).

Minimal reproducer (the new test): dense `sm120_matmul` through `jit_from_cudnn_graph` with
`CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2`, bf16 A/B, M = N = K = 128, fp32 intermediate and compute, fp32
output `y = mod(C, x)` (or `mod(x, C)`) with `x` an fp32 per-element aux. `A` is the identity, so `C` holds exactly the
chosen bf16 values. Values that differ bitwise from fmod on develop 24a8cd43:

| `mod(C, x)` operand group | wrong on develop |
|---|---|
| `k / 0.1f` rounds up to `10 k`, `k = 1..256` and `-1..-64` | 320 of 320 |
| `\|C / x\| >= 2**23` (`2**25 .. 3 * 2**50` by `-3, 0.7, 1.3, 2.9`) | 19 of 24 |
| `x = +-inf` | 8 of 8 (NaN) |
| exact negative multiples (`-0` expected) | 3 of 3 (`+0`) |
| `C / x` overflows | 2 of 2 (`-inf`) |
| `C mod 6.2831855`, `C` in `[1e6, 1e8]` | 79 of 256 |
| `x = 0` (NaN expected) | 0 of 2 |
| small quotients, `\|C / x\| <= 16` | 1 of 128 (`mod(-8, 0.5) = +0`) |

For `mod(x, C)`: 84 of 256 phases `x` in `[1e6, 1e8]` mod `bf16(2 pi)`, 3 of 3 large or overflowing quotients, and the same
signed-zero case. With this change every value matches fmod bitwise.

`arith.remf` is the right lowering: it states fmod semantics in the IR instead of approximating them. On SM120 and SM100 it
compiles to the exact fmodf expansion (a quotient estimate corrected through an exact FMA remainder, a reduction loop once
`|a / b| > 2**23`, and `copysign` for the sign of `a`), with no `div.rn.f32` and no floor (PTX counts under Testing). The
audit also ran it against `math.fmod` on 358,400 operand pairs on SM120, including `+-0`, subnormal, `+-inf` and NaN
operands, with no difference, and the random-operand sweep under Testing found none in 524,288 more. Patching the old form
(for example with a remainder correction step) would still need special cases for infinite divisors, quotient overflow and
signed zeros.

The change is outside `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/` because, since #1993, the epilogue op emitter exists only in the
shared `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`: both families' `generate()` call the shared `_emit_pointwise_dag`
(`sm120/epilogue_codegen.py:827`, `sm100/epilogue_codegen.py:498`), which, like the shared `generate_mainloop`, reaches it
through `_emit_op`. There is no per-family copy to fix instead.

Found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding G4.1).

## Related issues

None.

Related PRs from the same audit:

- #2022 (G4.4, INT32-compute epilogue ops): on SM120 it declines an INT32-compute `mod`, the case this PR leaves on the old
  form.
- These open PRs edit other hunks of the same shared `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`: #2018 (B09, comparisons
  in `_emit_binary_ext`), #2026 (G4.3, `relu_backward` in `_emit_binary_ext`), #2009 (B10, relu slope and clip in
  `_emit_binary_ext` and `_emit_op`), #2012 (G4.2, relu NaN propagation in `_emit_op`), #2025 (B11, tanh / elu / softplus in
  `_emit_op`), #2022 (`gen_index` in `_emit_op` and `_emit_pointwise_dag`), #2014 (B13, `_emit_round`) and #2013 (B14, the
  reduction AVG divisor). `git merge-tree` merges each of their current heads with this branch without conflicts.

## API and compatibility impact

- No API change. FlashInfer's exported Frost graphs contain no `mod`.
- Numerics: an fp32-compute `mod` now returns exact C fmod in every epilogue that reaches the emitter. On SM120 that is all
  six templates (dense and block-scale matmul, MoE grouped matmul and its swap-AB form, MoE grouped block-scale matmul and its
  swap-AB form) and the split-K reduction epilogue; SM120 has no mainloop fusion. Results that were already exact, such as
  the quotients below 10 drawn by the existing sweep, are unchanged except for the sign of exact-zero remainders.
- Native cuDNN parity (AGENTS.md Rule 9): on every operand group of the new test, FROST now gives the same bits as native
  cuDNN. They still differ on subnormals, and that predates this change: native cuDNN flushes subnormal operands and results
  to zero (a subnormal divisor gives NaN, a subnormal dividend or exact remainder gives `+-0`), while FROST computes exact
  fmod on them; develop's FROST kernel did not flush either. In the random-operand sweep under Testing every native
  difference from fmod is one of these subnormal cases. The new test does not pin subnormal behaviour.
- SM100: the emitter is shared, so the SM100 family's generated code changes the same way: every SM100 template epilogue,
  the split-K reduction epilogue and the `sm100_matmul_mainloop.py` mainloop-fusion transform (a `mod` with a scalar divisor
  on A or B). Both kinds were compile-checked for `sm_100a` on the SM120 host (see Testing); nothing ran on SM100 hardware.
  The new test's two SM100 cases (the dense SM100 template, gated by `requires_sm100`) give SM100 CI a bitwise check of the
  changed path; they compile for `sm_100a` but have not run. The existing SM100 `mod` case,
  `test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py::test_pointwise_mode_coverage[mod]` (quotients below about 10, bf16 output, tolerance
  5e-2, 0.2% mismatch budget), still exercises the path on SM100 CI but cannot detect this defect.
- INT32 compute is unchanged: a `mod` node with `compute_data_type=INT32` keeps the old form and still fails at build with
  the same `DSLRuntimeError` (`'arith.addf' op operand #1 must be floating-point-like, but got 'vector<8xi32>'`).
  INT32-compute epilogue ops are a separate audit finding (G4.4, #2022, which declines an INT32-compute `mod` on SM120).
  Emitting `%` there would select `arith.remsi`, whose zero-divisor and overflow cases are undefined.
- Performance: the fmodf expansion is longer than the old divide-and-floor sequence and adds a short data-dependent loop
  for `|a / b| > 2**23`. Only graphs with a `mod` node are affected. Not measured.
- Chains with `mod` render different kernel source, so their cached kernels are rebuilt once.

## Testing

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN
9.24, frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. All pytest commands from `test/python`.

Regression test, RED on develop (a copy of 24a8cd43's `python/cudnn` and `test/python` with only the new test added, own
kernel caches) and GREEN on this branch:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_epilogue_mod.py -rs
# develop 24a8cd43: 2 failed, 2 skipped in 0.52s
#   [sm120-mod_C_x] 432 of 16384 differ from fmod (per-group counts in the table above)
#   [sm120-mod_x_C] 88 of 16384 differ from fmod
# this branch:      2 passed, 2 skipped in 0.47s
# both: SKIPPED [2] needs a Blackwell-family GPU (100 <= SM < 120), have sm_120  (the sm100-* cases)
```

The SM120 cases are collected by `-k sm120`, the SM100 cases by `-k sm100`, and all four by `-k frost` and the default
`-m L0` sweep.

Related existing tests:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost -k sm120
# develop 24a8cd43: 1 failed, 1036 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected, 201 warnings in 292.75s
# this branch:      1 failed, 1038 passed, 82 skipped, 9791 deselected in 13.34s
#   (warm kernel cache, so the time is not comparable with the cold develop run)
```

The two extra passes are the new test's SM120 cases; its two SM100 cases are deselected. The one failure,
`test_matmul.py::test_sm120_epi_vec_clamp_and_stg_only`, fails the same way on develop (`_use_tma_store_epi(chain, cfg100)`
is False for the SM100 config on an SM120 GPU) and has no `mod`.

Host-side codegen tests that render epilogues and mainloop transforms through `_emit_op` (their SM100 GPU cases skip on
SM120):

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_multi_gemm.py gemm/frost/test_matmul_mainloop_fusion.py gemm/frost/test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py
# develop 24a8cd43: 22 passed, 493 skipped in 0.89s
# this branch:      22 passed, 493 skipped in 0.84s
```

Ad hoc checks (scripts not committed):

- Every SM120 path that reaches the emitter, values differing bitwise from fmod. GEMM results are small integers (exact);
  divisors alternate between `0.1f` and `U[0.5, 1.5)`, except in the two MoE block-scale rows, where they alternate between
  `0.1f` and random fp32 bit patterns:

  | SM120 path | develop | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | dense, scalar divisor (`0.1f`) | 24467 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, per-row divisor | 12218 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, per-column divisor | 12223 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, per-element divisor | 12216 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, in-chain divisor `mod(C, C * x)` | 7275 / 24576 | 0 |
  | dense, split-K 2 (reduction epilogue) | 12237 / 24576 | 0 |
  | MoE grouped matmul (NONE), E = 2 | 16285 / 32768 | 0 |
  | MoE grouped matmul (NONE), swap-AB | 16301 / 32768 | 0 |
  | MXFP8 dense block-scale matmul | 8154 / 16384 | 0 |
  | MXFP8 MoE grouped block-scale matmul (NONE), E = 2, per-element divisor | 23130 / 32768 | 0 |
  | MXFP8 MoE grouped block-scale matmul (NONE), swap-AB | 23191 / 32768 | 0 |

- Native cuDNN: the new test's two graphs built through the public graph API without the FROST opt-in (heuristic modes A and
  FALLBACK, plan list headed by `eng10_k24=25`), executed on the same operands: 0 values differ from fmod in every group.
- Random operands: 524,288 pairs through the new test's two graphs (16 draws of 16,384 per direction; `C` random finite
  normal bf16 values, `x` random fp32 bit patterns with a quarter replaced by near-integer quotients). This branch's FROST
  kernel matches fmod bitwise on all of them. Native cuDNN (same plan list) differs on 8,487, all subnormal cases: all 5,485
  subnormal divisors give NaN, and all 720 subnormal dividends and all 2,282 subnormal exact remainders of normal operands
  give `+-0` with the sign of fmod; none of the other 515,801 pairs differs. Develop's FROST kernel differs on 162,048 pairs,
  none of them a flush: it returns all 720 subnormal dividends exactly and no NaN for a subnormal divisor.
- `mod` with `compute_data_type=INT32` on the dense template: develop and this branch both fail at build with the same
  `DSLRuntimeError` (unchanged, see above).
- PTX instruction counts of the new test's SM120 kernel (`sm_120a`) and of the two SM100 kernels below (`sm_100a`, the two
  kernels' counts summed):

  | instruction | `sm_120a` develop | `sm_120a` this branch | `sm_100a` develop | `sm_100a` this branch |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `div.rn.f32` | 64 | 0 | 192 | 0 |
  | `cvt.rmi.f32.f32` (floor) | 192 | 0 | 576 | 0 |
  | `div.approx.f32` | 0 | 64 | 0 | 192 |
  | `cvt.rzi.f32.f32` | 0 | 128 | 0 | 384 |
  | `fma.rz.f32` | 0 | 64 | 0 | 192 |
  | `copysign.f32` | 0 | 64 | 0 | 192 |

- SM100 compile check (no launch: an `sm_100a` kernel cannot run here). The process runs the sm100 tree
  (`CUDNN_FRONTEND_GEMM_ARCH_FAMILY=sm100`, arch probe pinned to 100 as `gemm_test_utils.plan_as_sm100` does) and compiles,
  with `--gpu-arch sm_100a` and `CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma`, a dense `sm100_matmul` epilogue
  `mod(C, x)` with an fp32 per-element divisor and an `sm100_matmul_mainloop` graph with `mod(A, s)` for a scalar `s`. Both
  compile on develop and on this branch; the generated source on this branch emits `_op_0 = _ba0 % _bb0` and
  `_op_900 = _ba900 % _bb900`. The new test's two SM100 cases, built the same way from the test's own graphs, `Plan` helper
  and config, also compile for `sm_100a` and emit `_op_0 = _ba0 % _bb0`.

Not tested: SM100-family hardware (none available here), so the new test's SM100 cases have not run.

@@ -171,6 +171,12 @@ def _emit_binary_ext(op: FusionOp, a_expr: str, b_expr: str, idx: int, new: str)
         return lines + la + lb + [f"{new} = {na} + {nb} - {na} * {nb}"], new
 
     if op.op == "mod":
+        if op.compute_dtype == "fp32":
+            # MOD is C fmod. `%` on Float32 vectors lowers to arith.remf, an exact fmodf. The form below,
+            # a - b * trunc(a / b), rounds the quotient first: it is off by |b| when a / b rounds up to an
+            # integer, can leave (-|b|, |b|) once |a / b| >= 2**25, and gives NaN for b = +-inf. It is kept
+            # only for INT32 compute, which fails at build today.
+            return lines + [f"{new} = {a} % {b}"], new
         q = f"_mq{idx}"
         lines.append(f"{q} = {a} / {b}")
         lp, sp = _step01(q, f"_{idx}mp")

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""The epilogue MOD op is C fmod (cuDNN's floating-point remainder; torch.fmod).
+
+fmod is exact, so the dense SM120 and SM100 templates are checked bitwise, signed zeros
+included, on the operands an emission of a - b * trunc(a / b) gets wrong: quotients that
+round up to an integer (k / 0.1f), |a / b| >= 2**23, an infinite divisor and a quotient
+that overflows. The sm100-family sweep in test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py draws quotients
+below ~10 and compares within a tolerance, so it cannot tell the two forms apart.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from gemm_test_utils import Plan, requires_sm100, requires_sm120, vp
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+import cudnn
+import cudnn.gemm.frost  # noqa: F401  — installs the cudnn.pygraph recorder hook
+from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+# The emitter is shared, so each family's dense template runs the same cases.
+_CONFIGS = [
+    pytest.param("CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2", marks=requires_sm120, id="sm120"),
+    pytest.param("CONFIG_sm100_128x128x128_128x128x32_cluster1x1_1ctamma", marks=requires_sm100, id="sm100"),
+]
+_M = _N = _K = 128
+_INF, _NAN = float("inf"), float("nan")
+
+
+def _mod_graph(aux_is_dividend: bool):
+    """C = A @ B, then mod(C, x) or mod(x, C) with x a per-element fp32 aux; fp32 output."""
+    g = cudnn.pygraph(io_data_type=cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16, intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT, compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    A = g.tensor(name="A", dim=[1, _M, _K], stride=[_M * _K, _K, 1])
+    B = g.tensor(name="B", dim=[1, _K, _N], stride=[_K * _N, 1, _K])
+    C = g.matmul(A=A, B=B, name="mm")
+    x = g.tensor(name="x", dim=[1, _M, _N], stride=[_M * _N, _N, 1], data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    y = g.mod(input0=x, input1=C) if aux_is_dividend else g.mod(input0=C, input1=x)
+    y.set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT).set_output(True)
+    return g
+
+
+def _bf16(values) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``values`` rounded to bf16, as fp32."""
+    return torch.as_tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+
+
+def _cases(aux_is_dividend: bool) -> list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """(label, GEMM values, fp32 aux values); the GEMM values are bf16-exact and finite."""
+    if aux_is_dividend:  # mod(x, C)
+        return [
+            ("x mod bf16(2 pi), |x / C| up to 2**24", torch.full((256,), 6.28125), torch.linspace(1e6, 1e8, 256)),
+            ("|x / C| >= 2**23, x / C overflows", torch.tensor([-3.0, 0.5, 2.0**-100]), torch.tensor([2.0**25, 3e38, 1e38])),
+            ("x = +-inf, NaN, -0", torch.full((4,), 3.0), torch.tensor([_INF, -_INF, _NAN, -0.0])),
+            ("small quotients", _bf16(torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, 128)), torch.linspace(-8, 8, 128)),
+        ]
+    k = torch.arange(1, 257, dtype=torch.float32)
+    big = torch.tensor([2.0**25, 3 * 2.0**24, 5 * 2.0**27, 7 * 2.0**30, 2.0**40, 3 * 2.0**50])
+    return [
+        ("k / 0.1f rounds up to 10 k", torch.cat([k, -k[:64]]), torch.full((320,), 0.1)),
+        ("|C / x| >= 2**23", big.repeat_interleave(4), torch.tensor([-3.0, 0.7, 1.3, 2.9]).repeat(6)),
+        ("x = +-inf", torch.tensor([3.0, -2.5, 100.0, 0.0]).repeat_interleave(2), torch.tensor([_INF, -_INF]).repeat(4)),
+        ("exact negative multiples give -0", torch.tensor([-4.0, -6.0, -2.0]), torch.tensor([2.0, 3.0, 0.5])),
+        ("C / x overflows", _bf16([1e38, -1e38]), torch.full((2,), 2.0**-100)),
+        ("C mod 2 pi", _bf16(torch.linspace(1e6, 1e8, 256)), torch.full((256,), 6.2831855)),
+        ("x = 0 gives NaN", torch.tensor([5.0, 0.0]), torch.zeros(2)),
+        ("small quotients", _bf16(torch.linspace(-8, 8, 128)), torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, 128)),
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("aux_is_dividend", [False, True], ids=["mod_C_x", "mod_x_C"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("config", _CONFIGS)
+def test_epilogue_mod_is_exact_fmod(config, aux_is_dividend):
+    plan = Plan(_mod_graph(aux_is_dividend), config=by_name(config))
+    cases = _cases(aux_is_dividend)
+    assert all(len(gemm_vals) == len(aux_vals) for _, gemm_vals, aux_vals in cases)
+    # The remaining positions hold (1, 1), whose fmod is 0.
+    sizes = [(label, len(gemm_vals)) for label, gemm_vals, _ in cases]
+    sizes.append(("(1, 1) filler", _M * _N - sum(n for _, n in sizes)))
+    c = torch.cat([gemm_vals for _, gemm_vals, _ in cases] + [torch.ones(sizes[-1][1])])
+    x = torch.cat([aux_vals for _, _, aux_vals in cases] + [torch.ones(sizes[-1][1])])
+    assert torch.equal(c.to(torch.bfloat16).float(), c)
+    # With A = I every dot has one nonzero product, so C is exactly B: C[m, n] = Bt[n, m].
+    a = torch.eye(_M, _K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).view(1, _M, _K)
+    bt = c.view(_M, _N).t().contiguous().to(torch.bfloat16).view(1, _N, _K).cuda()
+    out = torch.full((1, _M, _N), -12345.0, device="cuda")
+    plan(vp(plan, a, bt, out, x.view(1, _M, _N).cuda()))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    dividend, divisor = (x, c) if aux_is_dividend else (c, x)
+    ref = torch.fmod(dividend.double(), divisor.double()).float()  # exact: an fp32 fmod is representable
+    got = out.flatten().cpu()
+    bad = ~((got.view(torch.int32) == ref.view(torch.int32)) | (got.isnan() & ref.isnan()))
+    report, start = [], 0
+    for label, n in sizes:
+        idx = bad[start : start + n].nonzero().flatten() + start
+        if len(idx):
+            j = int(idx[0])
+            report.append(
+                f"{label}: {len(idx)} of {n} differ, e.g. mod({dividend[j].item()!r}, {divisor[j].item()!r}) = {got[j].item()!r}, fmod = {ref[j].item()!r}"
+            )
+        start += n
+    assert not report, f"{int(bad.sum())} of {got.numel()} differ from fmod:\n  " + "\n  ".join(report)

No actionable defect found. The shared FP32 remainder emitter now matches fmod for the tested rounding boundaries, large quotients, infinite divisors, and signed-zero results. Validation covers both compiler families on native SM100 and the SM100 mainloop transform, including the clean combination with the current base. The pre-existing INT32 path is unchanged.

Validation: Reviewed both changed files and traced the shared emitter through both epilogue families and SM100 mainloop generation. Four exact-value cases passed on native SM100: both operand orders through the SM100 and SM120 compiler families. Each checks 16,384 outputs, comparing non-NaN bits, including signed zeros, and matching NaN locations against a CPU double-precision fmod reference. Restoring the base emitter on the same SM100 route reproduced 432 and 88 mismatching values in the two operand orders; the changed emitter had none. On an isolated combination with the current base, 38 pointwise tests passed. Independent mainloop checks on A and B passed for divisors 0.1, -3, infinity and 2**-100 with K=136: CPU reference agreement and paired bit-identical outputs across 16 CUDA graph replays. GEMM/FROST pipeline77576184 is running for this head. It covers the existing SM100 MOD path; the two new SM120-marked cases will skip in that lane.

Limitations: No native SM120 execution, independent MoE/block-scale MOD execution, or performance measurement. The exact remainder can cost more than the old approximation, especially for large quotients; no speed claim is made. No full native-backend parity claim for subnormal divisors or INT32 compute. Repeatability evidence covers the tested configurations.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
